title: Georgia Man Charged in Hit-and-Run Death of Toddler
excerpt: Rohitbhai Patel, 67, of Snellville faces felony charges after a 3-year-old boy was struck and killed on Winder Highway in Lawrenceville.
body:
Lawrenceville police arrested Rohitbhai Patel, 67, of Snellville, Georgia, on May 9 — nearly two weeks after a predawn hit-and-run killed a 3-year-old boy named Maxence on Winder Highway. Patel now faces felony charges that carry serious prison time under Georgia law.

**What happened on April 26:**
Officers responded at about 5:13 a.m. to reports of a missing child at an apartment complex on East Crogan Street, and while searching the area, found the child lying unresponsive in the roadway along Winder Highway near Stanley Court. Despite immediate life-saving efforts by officers on scene, the child was pronounced dead by the Gwinnett County Fire Department.

**How investigators cracked the case:**
Investigators from the department's Accident Investigation Unit used law enforcement databases and other investigative resources to identify the suspect vehicle as a blue 2008 Honda CR-V, and with assistance from the Criminal Investigation Division, later located the vehicle at a nearby warehouse and identified Patel as the suspected driver. Patel had allegedly continued working after the collision. He faces charges of felony hit-and-run under O.C.G.A. section 40-6-270 and second-degree vehicular homicide under O.C.G.A. section 40-6-393.1.

**The broader danger on Winder Highway:**
Residents told WSB-TV that drivers regularly tear through that stretch of Winder Highway and that worries about pedestrian safety are nothing new. The AAA Foundation for Traffic Safety reports that hit-and-run crashes made up roughly 15% of police-reported collisions in 2023, a record high, with pedestrians representing a significant share of those victims.

**What to watch:**
The Lawrenceville Police Department says the investigation remains active and ongoing, and anyone with information is urged to contact authorities. Patel's arraignment and the progression of felony charges through Gwinnett County courts will be the next critical milestones to follow.
